note: Short plain-English summaries of each standard, written for parents. The official wording is at the source links. 'app: false' marks standards a game cannot check on its own (speaking in a group, presentations, longer writing projects); they are listed so the coverage report is honest, and are left out of the coverage percentage. 'review: true' marks standards from another grade that the game practices for review; they are not counted either.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Understand a multiplication equation as a comparison: 35 is 5 times as many as 7.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Solve word problems with multiplicative comparison ('times as many'), telling it apart from additive comparison ('more than').

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Solve multi-step word problems with whole numbers and all four operations, including remainders; check answers with estimation.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Find factor pairs for numbers 1–100; know multiples; tell prime from composite.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Make a number or shape pattern that follows a rule and notice features of the pattern.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: A digit in one place is worth ten times what it would be in the place to its right.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Read and write multi-digit numbers in numerals, words and expanded form; compare them with >, = and <.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers fluently with the standard method.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Multiply up to a 4-digit number by a 1-digit number, and two 2-digit numbers, using place value and area models.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Divide up to 4-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers, with remainders.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Explain why fractions are equivalent and make equivalent fractions.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Compare two fractions with different numerators and denominators.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, including word problems.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Multiply a fraction by a whole number, including word problems.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Write a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 and add the two.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Compare two decimals to hundredths.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Know relative sizes of units (km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz; l, ml; hr, min, sec) and convert larger units to smaller ones.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Solve word problems about distance, time, volume, mass and money, including fractions and decimals.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Use the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world problems.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Make and read a line plot with fractions of a unit.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Understand angles as turns measured in degrees.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Measure and draw angles with a protractor.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Angle measures add up; find an unknown angle in a diagram.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Draw and find points, lines, segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Sort 2-D shapes by parallel or perpendicular lines and angle size; recognize right triangles.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Find lines of symmetry.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Make sense of problems and keep at them.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Explain your reasoning and find mistakes in other people's reasoning.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Tell and write time to the nearest minute; solve elapsed-time problems in minutes.

standards.subject: math
standards.summary: Draw and read scaled picture graphs and bar graphs.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Use details and examples from a story to explain what it says and what you can infer.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Find the theme of a story, play or poem and summarize it.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Describe a character, setting or event in depth using details from the text.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Figure out what words and phrases mean, including words from mythology.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Explain differences between poems, plays and prose (verse, rhythm, cast of characters, stage directions).

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Compare points of view, including first- and third-person narration.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Connect the text of a story to a visual or spoken version of it.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Compare similar themes and topics in stories from different cultures.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Read and understand grade 4–5 literature by the end of the year (reading range over the whole year).

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Use details and examples from an informational text to explain what it says and what you can infer.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Find the main idea, explain how details support it, and summarize.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Explain events, steps or ideas in a historical, scientific or technical text: what happened and why.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Figure out the meaning of subject words in a grade 4 informational text.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Describe how a text is organized: time order, comparison, cause and effect, problem and solution.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Compare a firsthand and a secondhand account of the same event.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Use charts, graphs, diagrams, timelines and other visuals to understand a text.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support points.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Combine information from two texts on the same topic.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Read and understand grade 4–5 informational texts by the end of the year (reading range over the whole year).

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Use letter-sound knowledge, syllables and word parts (roots, prefixes, suffixes) to read unfamiliar words.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Read aloud accurately and smoothly, with expression (checked by a grown-up: see Reading fluency in Grown-ups).

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Write opinion pieces with reasons and facts.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Write informative texts: topic sentence, grouped details, linking words, conclusion.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Write stories with dialogue, description, time order and an ending.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Produce clear, organized writing that fits the task and audience (longer pieces, checked by a teacher).

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Plan, revise and edit writing.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Use technology to publish writing and type at least one page in one sitting.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Do short research projects on different parts of a topic.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Gather information from experience, print and digital sources; take notes and list sources.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Use evidence from texts to support analysis and research.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Write routinely over short and long time frames.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Take part in group discussions, following rules and building on others' ideas.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Paraphrase information heard aloud or presented in pictures, numbers or other media.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker gives for a point.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Report on a topic or tell a story aloud, clearly and at a good pace.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Add audio recordings or visuals to presentations.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Speak formally or informally depending on the situation.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Grammar: relative pronouns and adverbs, -ing verb tenses, can/may/must, adjective order, prepositional phrases, complete sentences, confusing words.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Capital letters, commas and quotation marks for speech and quotations, comma before 'and/but/or', spelling.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Choose precise words, punctuation for effect, and formal or informal English.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Figure out unknown words from context, Greek and Latin word parts, and dictionaries.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Similes, metaphors, idioms, proverbs, synonyms and antonyms.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Learn and use grade-level academic and subject words, including words for actions, emotions and states of being.

standards.subject: ela
standards.summary: Explain what nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs do in a sentence.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: The faster an object moves, the more energy it has.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Energy moves from place to place by sound, light, heat and electric currents.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: When objects collide, energy changes (motion into sound and heat).

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Design a device that changes energy from one form to another.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Waves have patterns of amplitude and wavelength and can make objects move.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Light reflecting off objects and entering the eye lets us see them.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Patterns can be used to send information (codes, signals).

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Plants and animals have inside and outside parts that help them survive, grow, behave and reproduce.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Animals take in information through their senses, process it in the brain and respond.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Rock layers and fossils show how a landscape changed over time.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Water, ice, wind, living things and gravity weather and erode rocks and land.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Maps show patterns of Earth's features: mountains, volcanoes, earthquakes, ocean trenches.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Energy and fuels come from natural resources; using them affects the environment.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Compare designs that reduce the damage from earthquakes, floods, tsunamis and volcanoes.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Define a simple design problem with criteria and limits.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Compare several possible solutions to a problem.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Plan fair tests and use the results to improve a design.

standards.subject: science
standards.summary: Earth's land, water, air and living things interact (includes the water cycle).

standards.subject: social
standards.summary: California's physical and human geography: maps, latitude and longitude, regions, landforms and climate.

standards.subject: social
standards.summary: California's first peoples, European exploration, and the Spanish missions, presidios and pueblos.

standards.subject: social
standards.summary: The Mexican period, ranchos, the Gold Rush and statehood in 1850.

standards.subject: social
standards.summary: How California grew: railroads, immigration, farming, water, industry and important people.

standards.subject: social
standards.summary: The U.S. and California constitutions and how federal, state and local governments work.
